subject: Post-discovery: Technical deep dive (ML/infra) - scheduling & agenda

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: Technical deep dive (ML/infra) - scheduling & agenda

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the discovery call this morning. Quick recap:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood for low-latency, high-throughput inference for your clinical notes summarization pipeline.
- Current constraints you called out: PII handling, VPC/private deployment options, and 200ms token latency targets for the hot path.
- Next step (agreed on the call): 60–90 minute technical deep dive with your ML and infra teams to validate integration patterns and performance expectations.

Proposed windows (PST):
- Thu Mar 4: 10:00–11:30 or 15:00–16:30
- Fri Mar 5: 09:00–10:30 or 10:00–11:30

Agenda suggestion (we can tweak):
1) Introductions & scope (5–10m)
2) Architecture deep dive: current pipeline + integration points (10–15m)
3) Redwood runtime & deployment options (30–40m) — Neha/Marcus will cover dedicated vs private and latency/cost tradeoffs
4) Security/compliance: SOC2, encryption, tenant isolation (10–15m)
5) Q&A + next steps + mutual action items (10–15m)

Attachments: redwood-technical-overview.pdf (high-level runtime + integration patterns). Also happy to share SOC2 summary ahead of the call.

Please let me know which window works and any additional folks you want on the invite. If you prefer, share a couple of times and I’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134

- Would like to include our infra lead (Anika Bose) and an IT security rep (cc'd) — they'll want to hear about private deployment and key management.
- Can you share the SOC2 summary and any network diagram we can review before the call?
- Also, can Neha/Marcus speak to expected baseline token latency and typical throughput for a 2–3k seq workload?

If you can confirm invite for Mar 5 10:00–11:30 PST, I’ll block it and send an Outlook invite.

Thanks,

Perfect — Mar 5, 10:00–11:30 PST is confirmed on our side. I’ll send a calendar invite once we lock attendees.

Per requests: attaching redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and sending a short pre-read link (Drive) for the runtime/network diagram: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-tech-overview

Neha and Marcus will cover token latency baselines and throughput expectations. Quick answers ahead of the call:
- Baseline P95 per-token latency on current production config (A100-class) is ~60–90ms for 2k tokens with batching; optimized configs and KV caching can reduce end-user latency considerably for hot paths.
- We’ll bring example perf numbers and a simple test plan (load, sample prompts, data residency options).

Agenda tweak proposal from our engineering team: add a short walk-through of your expected traffic patterns and example prompt shapes (10m) ahead of the runtime deep dive — helps us tune the demo.

I’ll include Anika (if you can share her email) and the IT security rep on the invite. Evelyn (cc'd) is our AE manager and will join the first 15 minutes to align on commercial milestones.

—
Camila

Thanks Camila — happy to join. Sanjay — quick note on prep from the engineering side:
- Please share one or two representative example prompts + average sequence lengths and expected QPS during peak. That will help us pick the right quantization/profile for the demo.
- We’ll present: runtime architecture, KV/prefix caching options, routing policies for multi-tenant + dedicated pools, and an expected performance matrix (latency vs cost).
- Marcus will run the demo portion showing a sample pipeline and integration hooks (we’ll keep it to ~25–30m).

If you have any internal requirements around audit logs, retention, or key management, drop those into the pre-read doc or send them to me directly so Marcus can address during the security section.

Looking forward to it — we’ll prepare a short slide + demo notebook and share before the call.

Neha Kapoor
